2023_21_troy_school_district_0623_draft_.paragraph: Troy School District's draft Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, prepared by the Business Services Department and transmitted October 3, 2023 by Deputy Superintendent Rick West and Director of Finance Kandice Moynihan, with an unmodified audit opinion from Plante & Moran. Combined governmental fund balance rose $187,034,376 to $237,688,462, driven almost entirely by the first $171,370,000 series of the $555 million bond Troy voters approved on November 8, 2022. The General Fund ended at $32,620,321, down $360,516, and the net position deficit narrowed to $(162,472,077) against a net pension liability of $340,447,659.

**Document**

Draft Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) of Troy School District, a Michigan school district in suburban Oakland County, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023. Prepared by the Department of Business Services at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; letter of transmittal dated October 3, 2023 from Deputy Superintendent Rick West and Director of Finance Kandice Moynihan. Plante & Moran, appointed by the Troy Board of Education, issued an unmodified opinion dated October 3, 2023; there were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards. ASBO International has awarded the district a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years ended June 30, 1989 through 2022.

**Government-wide position and results (governmental activities)**

| Measure | 2023 | 2022 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Total assets | $473.1M | $275.7M |
| Deferred outflows of resources | $131.9M | $65.1M |
| Total liabilities | $700.4M | $382.9M |
| Deferred inflows of resources | $67.1M | $136.2M |
| Net investment in capital assets | $92.4M | $82.1M |
| Unrestricted net position | $(263.7)M | $(266.6)M |
| Total net position (deficit) | $(162,472,077) | $(178,223,715) |

Total revenue was $224.6 million against $208,835,697 of expenses, producing a $15,751,638 increase in net position. Expenses by function: instruction $123,107,488; support services $69,275,079; community services $4,687,389; interest $4,392,161; food services $4,175,797; athletics $2,361,149; other debt costs $836,634. Program revenue totaled $8,064,517 in charges for services and $60,617,779 in operating grants; general revenue included $86,465,321 of unrestricted state aid and $61,365,284 of property taxes ($38,007,427 general operating, $18,910,537 debt service, $4,447,320 capital projects).

**Fund results**

| Fund | Balance 6/30/2023 | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| General Fund | $32,620,321 | $(360,516) |
| 2023 Capital Projects Fund | $188,680,666 | +$188,680,666 |
| Nonmajor governmental funds | $16,387,475 | $(1,285,774) |
| Total governmental funds | $237,688,462 | +$187,034,376 |

Governmental funds took in $235,631,022 and spent $238,943,740; other financing sources of $190,347,094 (face value $171,370,000 plus $18,977,094 premium) produced the net increase. General Fund unassigned fund balance of $32,034,595 equals 16.9 percent of 2023 general operating expenditures, against a board policy minimum of 15 percent. Special revenue fund balances rose from $5.9 million to $9.7 million; capital projects funds rose $182.7 million; debt service funds rose $0.9 million.

**Budget versus actual, General Fund**

Original budgeted revenue of $172,213,454 was amended to $189,304,235 (actual $189,049,577); budgeted expenditures went from $176,243,584 to $189,751,106 (actual $189,410,093). Budgeted revenue was raised $17.1 million, chiefly state categorical aid (full Section 31a At Risk funding for hold-harmless districts and one-time Section 147c2 money) and $1.3 million of federal ESSER II and Section 11t funds; $1.2 million of transfers from special revenue funds was removed. The final amendment was adopted in June 2023.

**Capital assets and debt**

Capital assets totaled $414,311,763 gross and $202,522,934 net of $211,788,829 accumulated depreciation and amortization, up about $3.5 million; additions were $13.6 million. Bonds outstanding grew from $116,165,000 to $271,570,000, plus $25,179,339 of unamortized premium. Standard & Poor's affirmed an AA/Stable rating in January 2023. Debt service to maturity totals $433,473,045 ($271,570,000 principal, $161,903,045 interest) through 2052.

**Enrollment and outlook**

Spring 2023 enrollment was 12,540 across twelve elementary schools, four middle schools, three high schools and International Academy East. The 2023-2024 budget assumed 12,282 students and a $458 per-pupil foundation allowance increase to $10,332. Board of Education: Karl Schmidt (President), Dr. Nicole Wilson (Vice President), Gary Hauff (Secretary), and trustees Vital Anne, Emina Alic, Dr. Nancy Philippart and Matt Haupt; Superintendent Richard Machesky, Ed.D.

**Identity, governance and audit**

Draft Annual Comprehensive Financial Report with Supplementary Information for Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, prepared by the Business Services Department at the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248-823-4000). The letter of transmittal, dated October 3, 2023, is signed by Rick West, Deputy Superintendent (rwest@troy.k12.mi.us, 248.823.4022) and Kandice Moynihan, Director of Finance. Board of Education: Karl Schmidt, President; Dr. Nicole Wilson, Vice President; Gary Hauff, Secretary; trustees Vital Anne, Emina Alic, Esq., Dr. Nancy Philippart and Matt Haupt, Esq. Administration: Richard Machesky, Ed.D., Superintendent; Rick West, Deputy Superintendent; Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent Secondary Instruction; Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent Elementary Instruction; John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent Employee Services. Plante & Moran issued an unmodified opinion dated October 3, 2023, with a companion Government Auditing Standards report the same date; there were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards, and Federal Awards Supplementary Information is issued under separate cover. ASBO International has awarded Certificates of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years 1989 through 2022 (the FY2022 certificate signed by John W. Hutchison, President, and Siobhan McMahon, CAE). The district is governed by an elected seven-member board and has no component units; subsequent events were evaluated through October 3, 2023.

**District profile**

More than 12,000 students attend twelve elementary schools, four middle schools, two traditional and one non-traditional high school, and International Academy East. Troy covers 26.61 square miles, is the largest city in Oakland County and 13th largest in Michigan, has roughly 80,000 residents and over 6,000 businesses with a market value over $12 billion, and more than 57 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. Thirteen schools have won the National Blue-Ribbon Award (Barnard, Bemis, Leonard, Martell, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass, Wattles, Larson, Boulan Park, Athens, Troy High and the International Academy); Athens and Troy High report graduation rates over 99 percent. The 2026 Strategic Plan, adopted by board resolution as successor to World Class 2020, rests on four pillars: Early Childhood to Career, Equity and Well-Being, Deep Learning, and Building Capacity. Facilities total 448.74 acres and 2,185,181 square feet plus 128.30 vacant acres, ranging from Troy High (73.13 acres, 343,207 sq ft, 1992, 2,086 students) and Athens High (50.00 acres, 398,426 sq ft, 1974, 1,533) to the Preschool/Early 5's and ECP building (13.60 acres, 72,000 sq ft, 2019, 208).

**Government-wide financial position**

Total assets were $473,162,019: cash and cash equivalents $40,006,840; due from other governments $29,359,729; other receivables $532,785; inventory $121,941; prepaid expenses $526,658; restricted assets $200,091,132; capital assets $202,522,934. Deferred outflows were $131,860,812 (deferred pension costs $105,458,305, deferred OPEB costs $26,091,791, deferred charges on bond refunding $310,716). Total liabilities were $700,412,673: accounts payable $5,568,084; due to other governmental units $6,727,622; accrued salaries and wages $9,974,718; accrued payroll taxes and fringe benefits $6,901,361; accrued interest $2,275,284; unearned revenue $3,778,838; noncurrent due within one year $21,572,288 and beyond one year $283,925,834; net pension liability $340,447,659; net OPEB liability $19,240,985. Deferred inflows were $67,082,235. Net position was $(162,472,077): net investment in capital assets $92,427,309; restricted for capital projects $5,617,158, food service $3,015,211 and debt service $155,414; unrestricted $(263,687,169), against $(178,223,715) a year earlier.

**Statement of activities**

Expenses of $208,835,697 broke down as instruction $123,107,488 (net $(81,620,566) after $474,025 of charges and $41,012,897 of operating grants); support services $69,275,079 (net $(51,698,123)); athletics $2,361,149; food services $4,175,797 (net positive $242,768); community services $4,687,389; interest $4,392,161; other debt costs $836,634. Net program expense was $(140,153,401). General revenue of $155,905,039 included property taxes of $38,007,427 (general), $18,910,537 (debt service) and $4,447,320 (capital projects); unrestricted state aid $86,465,321; federal grants $41,954; interest and investment earnings $4,143,480; student activities $3,370,682; other $823,344; and a $(305,026) loss on sale of capital assets.

**Governmental funds and budget**

Combined fund balance reached $237,688,462, up $187,034,376 from $50,654,086. Revenue of $235,631,022 comprised local $77,767,307, state $129,932,089, federal $16,849,413 and interdistrict $11,082,213. Expenditures of $238,943,740 comprised instruction $127,082,439, support services $64,776,167, athletics $2,381,909, food services $4,114,838, community services $4,772,649, principal $15,965,000, interest $3,424,055, other debt costs $836,634 and capital outlay $15,590,049. The General Fund closed at $32,620,321 with $32,034,595 unassigned (16.9 percent of operating expenditures versus a 15 percent policy floor); the 2023 Capital Projects Fund at $188,680,666; nonmajor funds at $16,387,475. Nonmajor ending balances include Food Service $3,015,211, Community Service $2,326,059, Troy Career Center $0, Preschool $1,883,979, Troy School and Student Activities $2,446,386, 2015 Refunding Debt $767,279, 2016 Debt $497,827, 2019 Debt $334,362, 2021 Refunding Series B $831,230, 2019 Capital Projects $1,685,663, Capital Maintenance $672,125 and Sinking Fund $1,927,354; the 2014 Debt Fund and 2021 Refunding Series A Fund ended at zero. Custodial funds held $95,845 of cash and $92,862 of net position. General Fund budgeted revenue was amended from $172,213,454 to $189,304,235 (actual $189,049,577) and expenditures from $176,243,584 to $189,751,106 (actual $189,410,093); revenue was raised $17.1 million on state categorical aid (Section 31a At Risk and one-time Section 147c2) plus $1.3 million of ESSER II and Section 11t funds, and $1.2 million of special revenue transfers was removed. Largest actual lines: basic programs $93,093,879, added needs $30,968,129, pupil support $14,256,909, operations and maintenance $13,909,481.

**Capital assets, debt and the bond program**

Gross capital assets rose from $400,750,723 to $414,311,763 (land $1,861,010; construction in progress $3,588,390; buildings and improvements $356,601,423; furniture and equipment $51,730,652; lease asset $530,288), net $202,522,934 after $211,788,829 of accumulated depreciation. Depreciation and amortization expense of $9,995,870 was charged to instruction $4,112,835, support services $5,668,498, community services $101,531, athletics $64,989 and food services $48,017. Construction commitments remaining totaled $32,963,954 ($28,019,164 in the 2023 Capital Projects Fund, $4,517,862 in the Sinking Fund, $426,928 in the 2019 Capital Projects Fund). General obligation bonds rose from $116,165,000 to $271,570,000; with $25,179,339 of premium, bonds payable were $296,749,339 and total long-term debt $305,498,122 (including $8,262,756 of compensated absences, $333,527 of leases for the Troy Career Center building and $152,500 of other termination benefits), of which $21,572,288 is due within a year. Issues outstanding: 2015 refunding ($31,930,000 original, 5.00 percent, May 1, 2026, $9,675,000); 2016 ($40,000,000, 2.94-4.50 percent, 2032, $30,550,000); 2018 ($7,125,000, 3.00-3.75 percent, 2040, $6,340,000); 2019 ($22,630,000, 5.00 percent, 2034, $18,325,000); 2020 ($6,100,000, 2.00 percent, 2035, $5,020,000); 2021 refunding ($33,315,000, 0.50-1.56 percent, 2028, $30,290,000); and 2023 ($171,370,000, 2.75-5.00 percent, May 1, 2052). Debt service to maturity is $433,473,045 ($271,570,000 principal, $161,903,045 interest), with $31,815,482 due in 2024. S&P affirmed AA/Stable in January 2023. Management cites $11.4 million of unqualified debt against a $694.6 million limit and $260.2 million of qualified debt; the legal debt margin schedule shows a $693,590,391 limit, $11,360,000 net debt subject to limit (1.64 percent) and a $682,230,391 margin. Voters approved $555 million on November 8, 2022, to be issued in three series over six years for projects spanning ten to twelve years; $4.4 million of sinking fund millage was collected in 2023.

**Deposits, MPSERS and other notes**

Nine financial institutions were designated and three used; $47,246,346 of bank deposits were uninsured and uncollateralized. Investments of $194,630,950 sat in the Michigan Liquid Asset Fund Cash Management Money Market Fund ($192,940,328, AAAm) and MILAF MAX Class ($1,690,622, AAAm). Restricted assets of $200,091,132 consist of unspent bond proceeds and interest $194,630,950, sinking fund taxes $3,059,083 and debt service taxes $2,401,099. Under the Michigan Public School Employees' Retirement System, the net pension liability of $340,447,659 and net OPEB liability of $19,240,985 were measured at September 30, 2022 (proportions 0.90524 and 0.90842 percent). Pension expense was $43,642,684 and an OPEB recovery of $6,981,694 was recognized. Pension contributions were $42,481,418, including $15,584,907 for the MPSERS UAAL stabilization rate and a one-time $9,076,463 Section 147c(2) payment; OPEB contributions were $7,430,175. The discount rate is 6.00 percent; at 5.00 percent the pension liability would be $449,264,431 and at 7.00 percent $250,777,736. Payables to the plans were $9,208,156 and $999,310. The district participates in the SET-SEG shared-risk pool; PA 198 of 1974 industrial facilities exemptions and brownfield agreements cut property tax revenue about $105,000, with roughly $90,000 reimbursed by the State. GASB Statement No. 101 takes effect for the year ending June 30, 2025.

**Statistical highlights**

Tax year 2022 taxable value was $4,623,935,940 (residential $3,099,545,240; commercial $979,250,150; industrial $255,866,910; personal property $289,273,640) at 50 percent of $9,247,871,880 estimated actual value, taxed at 26.1344 mills; the homestead direct rate was 8.1344 mills and non-homestead 23.0651, including 18.0000 operating, 4.1000 debt and 0.9651 sinking fund. The $61,388,795 levy was 97.89 percent collected currently and 99.68 percent overall. Somerset Collections led taxpayers at $60,876,330. Net general bonded debt of $294,318,642 equals 6.37 percent of taxable value and $3,351 per capita on a population of 87,830; overlapping debt of $26,012,612 (City of Troy $11,085,101, Oakland County $12,241,514, Oakland ISD $2,685,998) plus $269,139,302 direct debt totals $295,151,914. William Beaumont Hospital was the largest employer (2,300) and the district second (1,331). The district employed 1,082 FTEs including 882 in instruction, with 855 teachers, an average teacher salary of $77,080, cost per pupil of $15,104, revenue per pupil of $15,076, 16.00 percent free/reduced meal eligibility and 74 buses.
